title: provider-assurance-evidence
description: Versioned, structured record of the canonical 10-item provider due-diligence checklist from docs/ai-data-privacy-and-model-security.md section 5 (issue #237, threat AI-07, ADR-0029). This is metadata/attestation REFERENCES only - it MUST NEVER carry a raw provider response, contract text, prompt/response content, or a secret/credential value. Each checklist item records a bounded verification status plus an opaque, non-secret evidence reference (e.g. a ticket, DPA record, or attestation identifier) - never the underlying document content. This schema documents the canonical shape; an equivalent `provider_assurance` object is embedded directly in `egress-decision-request.schema.json` (this validator subset does not support `$ref`, so the shape is intentionally duplicated rather than cross-referenced - the two must be kept in sync by hand). This record makes no certification, audit, or legal-compliance claim - it is engineering evidence that due diligence was performed and recorded, not a guarantee of provider behavior.

schema_version.description: The provider-assurance-evidence contract version this record was authored against. An evaluator that does not recognize this version must fail closed (deny) rather than guess at semantics.

provider_id.description: An opaque provider/profile identifier - never a credential. Must match the corresponding `provider_posture.provider_id` used in the same egress decision.

assessed_at.description: UTC timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) the checklist was last assessed/reviewed. Freshness policy (how stale an assessment may be before it is treated as unverified) is operator-defined and enforced by the caller, not by this schema.

assessment_reference.description: Optional opaque reference to the assessment record (e.g. a ticket, DPA register entry, or vendor-review identifier) - a pointer only, never the document content itself.

items.description: The 10-item due-diligence checklist from docs/ai-data-privacy-and-model-security.md section 5. Items 1-9 must be `verified` before a cloud destination can be approved; item 10 (private-networking/zero-retention options) is 'where available' and may instead be `not_applicable`.

data_categories_and_purpose.description: Checklist item 1: data categories and purpose of processing are documented.

controller_processor_roles.description: Checklist item 2: controller/processor (or equivalent) roles are documented.

retention_and_deletion.description: Checklist item 3: retention and deletion behavior is documented.

training_use.description: Checklist item 4: use for training/model improvement is documented. A provider's 'not used for training' claim alone is not sufficient - this item records that the claim was independently assessed and recorded, not merely restated.

abuse_monitoring_human_access.description: Checklist item 5: abuse-monitoring and human/operations access conditions are documented.

subprocessors_and_transfer_locations.description: Checklist item 6: subprocessors and transfer/geographic processing locations are documented.

encryption_and_tenant_isolation.description: Checklist item 7: encryption in transit/at rest and tenant isolation is documented.

contractual_dpa_terms.description: Checklist item 8: contractual/DPA terms and applicable legal basis are documented.

incident_notification_and_audit.description: Checklist item 9: incident notification and audit evidence terms are documented.

private_networking_zero_retention_option.description: Checklist item 10: private-networking/zero-retention options, where available. This item alone may be `not_applicable` when the provider offers no such option; every other item must be `verified`.
